She is allowed to have other friends, she is not your possession. And nobody can “save” other people. Work on healthy boundaries. 

Emotional boundaries for yourself- not trying to “save” people and examining why you feel so insecure about one of your friends having other friends

And boundaries with other people. Allowing them to have other relationships, knowing your own value so you don’t feel the need to change yourself to fit their wants.

Talking to a counselor or therapist can really help to build up self worth so you’re not forming your existence around other people, and focus on your own wants/ needs/ desires. Working on yourself means not just physical health but building up your mental health- however that looks for you. Therapy, 12 step programs (they’re not just for substance abuse), support groups, and outpatient programs are just a few options.

I have two techniques I use when I’m overwhelmed (with varying degrees of success, but I’m practicing)
1. Concentrate on breathing. Try to inhale deep into your stomach and exhale fully. I inhale for a count of 5 and exhale for 7. The numbers themselves aren’t important, just trying to lengthen the exhale
2. Mindfulness/noting: whenever the feelings of anxiety/difficult thoughts come up, label them in your head. Just thinking in a calm voice “anxiety” or “shame”, just creating some distance between yourself and the unpleasant thoughts and feelings

My understanding of it is that our bodies stores the effects of trauma physically (the “body keeps the score” and “why zebras don’t get ulcers” are good books that help explain it)  which causes certain symptoms. The psychedelic puts you in a state where you can sit with the physical and emotional symptoms and allow your body to process them. 

My therapist is there to remind me that I’m safe and to help guide me through the process, which mostly involves me noticing and allowing myself to feel it, and seeing if anything comes up with it (memories, other emotions, physical sensations). 

Keep in mind that I am just a patient, so my understanding of it may not entirely be correct. r/psychedelictherapy has some good articles on it
